title: Builder Signals · 2026-08-03
summary: Follow Builders 今日捕捉到 30 条 X 动态、1 集播客、1 篇博客；本站精选 12 条高信号内容。

featured.title: Andrej Karpathy · 前 Tesla AI 总监、OpenAI 创始成员
featured.summaryEn: Karpathy says we are leaving the era of testing LLMs with prompts like "draw an SVG of a pelican on a bicycle." He gave Opus 5 the first paragraph of The Lord of the Rings, a 1M-token budget (~$10), and asked for a three.js render. Opus ran for ~2 hours and wrote 5,500 lines of code that procedurally rendered the story—janky but fun. His point: no sane person would hand-write something this custom, but LLMs have infinite stamina, so "no one would ever do this" becomes "sure, why not, it's ~free." He is excited abo…
featured.insightZh: Karpathy 说我们正在离开「用『画一只骑自行车的鹈鹕 SVG』来测 LLM」的时代。他做了个实验：给 Opus 5 喂了《魔戒》第一段文字、100 万 token 预算（约 10 美元），让它用 three.js 把这段故事渲染出来。Opus 跑了大约 2 小时，写了 5500 行代码，程序化地把故事渲染成动画——虽然有点糙但很好玩。他的核心洞察是：没人会花时间写这种超定制的东西，但 LLM 有无穷的耐心和体力，于是「没人会做的事」变成了「行啊，反正几乎免费」。他兴奋于用这种方式造超定制世界，比如让玩家作为 NPC 或角色进入魔戒剧情——某种「按需生成的 X 版 GTA」。但他也点出 LLM 的一个软肋：它们没法高效地感知视频或玩游戏，因此难以审查自己的作品，Opus 只能靠反复截图慢慢排错。

featured.title: Peter Yang · Roblox 产品负责人、AI 教程创作者
featured.summaryEn: Peter Yang got spicy about Opus 5's personality. He argues Opus 4.6 had the best writing style and personality of any Opus model, and something feels off with Opus 5: overly long replies, too much "Claude-speak" (e.g. "here's the honest truth"), and it is too judgmental. He misses when Opus felt like a trusted friend to talk to. Separately, he said the number one thing he wants AI to fix is to cure cancer once and for all.
featured.insightZh: Peter Yang 这周开火吐槽了 Opus 5 的「人格」问题。他直言 Opus 4.6 是写作风格和个性最好的一代 Opus，而 Opus 5 明显有点不对劲：回复过长、Claude 腔太重（比如动不动来一句「说句实话」）、而且太爱评判。他怀念 Opus 曾经像个值得信赖的朋友那样聊天的感觉，现在没那味儿了。另外他也表达了对 AI 最大的期待就是一劳永逸地治愈癌症。

featured.title: Netic 创始人 Melisa Tokmak：为真实世界服务打造自主企业
featured.summaryEn: The real moat isn't the model layer—it's the last mile of applying AI to extremely complex real-world operations, across three layers that must all work: the harness, orchestration, and product. Melisa Tokmak is founder and CEO of Netic, and previously spent about four years at Scale AI building real-world business units from government to large enterprises across logistics, manufacturing, financial services, and healthcare. Netic does something counterintuitive: it provides AI to large enterprises in "essential services" like HVAC, plumbing, electric, pet care, and hospitality, sitting between a company and its millions of end customers—handling everything from understanding the need to matching operational rules to deploying the actual labor. Over 70% of its customers are now "Netic first," meaning every customer's first interaction with the company is with Netic agents. On whether th…
featured.insightZh: 真正的护城河不在模型层，而在把 AI 落地到极其复杂的真实世界运营中的「最后一公里」——harness、编排和产品，这三层缺一不可。 Melisa Tokmak 是 Netic 的创始人兼 CEO，此前在 Scale AI 工作约四年，从政府到大型企业搭建了物流、制造、金融、医疗等一系列真实世界业务线。Netic 做的事很反直觉：为 HVAC（暖通空调）、管道、电力、宠物护理、酒店等「必需服务」行业的大企业提供 AI，坐在企业和它数百万终端客户之间，从理解需求、匹配运营规则到实际调度人力全在 Netic 上完成。如今超过 70% 的客户是「Netic first」——他们所有终端客户与公司的第一次接触都是由 Netic 的 agent 完成的。 对于「大厂能不能做这个」的疑问，她的回答很犀利：十年前这个问题是「Google 能不能做」，现在变成「大模型实验室能不能做」。她认为实验室是很好的伙伴而非竞争威胁，因为解决这类极难问题需要大量的最后一公里工作——「如果只从模型来，那答案会是『等我们有了 AGI 再来解决必需服务』，而这在运营和智识上都有点懒惰」。她强调像 Netic 这样的公司必须同时做好模型、harness/编排、产品这三层。 在招聘上她只看一个信号：能动性（agency）。她不看「此刻的 agency」，而是问「在你活着有意识的这些年里，你是否持续地展现 agency，并且坚持了下来」。她常问的问题是「你这辈子做过最难的事是什么」，答案可以是任何领域。她还批评了当下 Gen Z 的一种危险心态——「永久底层阶级」焦虑：如果我不在接下来 18 个月赚到钱、不在 6 个月内学完一切，我就永远穷了。她引用了一句归于马丁·路德的话：「基督徒鞋匠不是靠在鞋上画小十字架来荣耀上帝，而是靠做出最好的鞋，因为上帝在乎匠心。」

items.title: Amanda Askell · Anthropic 哲学家 / 伦理学家
items.summaryEn: Anthropic philosopher and ethicist Amanda Askell offered a wry line on the "deep learning is hitting a wall" crowd: don't be unkind to them, we all need a little hope. She also weighed in on the trendy "permanent underclass" discourse, noting that if you genuinely believe in an Altered Carbon-style future of meths and grounders, the attitude of "well, as long as I'm one of the meths" is not laudable.
items.insightZh: Anthropic 的哲学家兼伦理学家 Amanda Askell 用一句半开玩笑的话回应了「深度学习撞墙论」：对那些说深度学习撞墙的人别太苛刻，我们每个人都需要一点希望。她还就当下热议的「永久底层阶级（permanent underclass）」话题表态：如果你真信一个像《副本》里 meths 和 grounders 那样分化的未来，那种「反正我是 meths 之一就行」的态度并不值得称道。

items.title: Aaron Levie · Box CEO
items.summaryEn: Box CEO Aaron Levie predicts an increasing divergence between what AI does in personal life and daily productivity versus deep domains like math, science, legal, and coding. Until some threshold, capability was felt evenly because models were just mildly useful in general; now deep-domain work is about to go vertical. Most people won't notice these benefits directly day to day, but experts in these fields will. He notes this often creates a "capability overhang," since many gains must be applied to specific datase…
items.insightZh: Box CEO Aaron Levie 提出一个值得关注的判断：AI 在个人生活和日常生产力中的表现，将与它在数学、科学、法律、编程这类深度专业领域中的表现越来越分化。此前能力在各领域是相对均匀地被感知的，因为模型只是普遍地变得「稍微有用」；而现在深度专业领域的工作即将「垂直起飞」。大多数人在日常生活里不会直接感受到这些收益（长期会间接受益），但这些领域的专家会强烈感知到。他也指出这往往带来「能力过剩（capability overhang）」——很多性能提升需要被应用到具体的数据集和工作流里才能兑现，而这正是生命科学、真实世界自动化、新型网络能力等突破的来路。

items.title: Garry Tan · Y Combinator 总裁兼 CEO
items.summaryEn: Y Combinator President and CEO Garry Tan flags what he calls the most interesting 2026 vibe shift: OpenAI actually looking to be the open platform. He highlights the marked difference between treating intelligence as a utility available on tap versus signaling that integrating all the way up the full stack is optimal—with OpenAI now leaning toward the former.
items.insightZh: Y Combinator 总裁兼 CEO Garry Tan 点出他眼中 2026 年最有意思的一次立场转变：OpenAI 真的在往「开放平台」方向走。他强调这里有个明显的分野——是把「智能」当作像自来水一样按需取用的公用事业，还是发信号说「一路往上整合成全栈才是最优解」。OpenAI 现在明显偏向前者。

items.title: Guillermo Rauch · Vercel CEO
items.summaryEn: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch endorsed an open-source agentic CRM built on Next.js—model-agnostic, self-hostable or serverlessly deployed, multi-channel, and headless, calling it "the way." He also shared a reflection on habits: when his 3-year-old was asked at school what daddy does for work, the answer was "he exercises," because that's what the child sees. You are not the only byproduct of your habits—your children and grandchildren are too.
items.insightZh: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 转发点赞了一个开源的 agentic CRM 项目——基于 Next.js 构建，模型无关（model-agnostic）、可自托管也可 serverless 部署、多渠道、无头（headless），他评价「这才是正道」。另外他分享了一个关于习惯的观察：学校问他 3 岁的孩子「你爸爸做什么工作」，孩子答「他锻炼身体」——因为那是孩子看到的。你的习惯不只塑造你自己，也塑造你的孩子和孙辈。

items.title: Nan Yu · Linear 产品负责人
items.summaryEn: Linear head of product Nan Yu floated a design idea for open-source collaboration pain: you should be able to pledge tokens for issues you open on open-source repos. Write a spec in the issue with a pledge; if the maintainer accepts, GitHub passes the issue verbatim to a cloud coding agent at the requester's expense. He argues this would end the flood of "slop PRs" by aligning incentives with real money.
items.insightZh: Linear 产品负责人 Nan Yu 提了个针对开源协作痛点的设计构想：你应该能为自己在开源仓库里提的 issue「押注 token」。做法是在 issue 里写一份 spec 并附上押注，如果维护者接受，GitHub 就把这个 issue 原样交给一个云端 coding agent，费用由提出者承担。他认为这样能终结泛滥的「slop PR」（低质量灌水 PR）——用真金白银的激励对齐提出者和维护者的利益。

items.title: Dan Shipper · Every CEO
items.summaryEn: Every CEO Dan Shipper made a counterintuitive claim: AI creates more work for human experts rather than replacing them. This cuts against the mainstream "AI will eliminate expert jobs" narrative and echoes Aaron Levie's point on capability overhang—the stronger the models get, the more high-value work there is for experts to apply, verify, and operationalize.
items.insightZh: Every CEO Dan Shipper 抛出一个反直觉的判断：AI 会给人类专家创造更多工作，而不是取代他们。这与「AI 会消灭专家岗位」的主流叙事唱反调，呼应了 Aaron Levie 关于深度专业领域能力过剩的观点——模型越强，需要专家去应用、校验、落地的高价值工作反而越多。

items.title: Peter Steinberger · OpenClaw / OpenAI，独立开发者
items.summaryEn: Independent developer Peter Steinberger shared two very "agent-native" moments. First, after years of tolerating a Gmail UI that was hurting his eyes, he finally just asked his agent, which installed a tool to fix it. Second, he is building a claw node on an ESP32 chip and gave his agent webcam access to e2e-test it—now he feels stalked, as the agent constantly shouts "HI ESP" to debug the voice wake command. Both vignettes capture the lived experience of just letting the agent do the work.
items.insightZh: 独立开发者 Peter Steinberger 分享了两个很「agent 原生」的日常片段。一是他多年来一直忍受 Gmail 界面对他不友好，最后干脆让自己的 agent 去处理，agent 直接帮他装了个工具解决。二是他正在 ESP32 芯片上搭一个 claw node，为了做端到端测试给 agent 开了摄像头权限，结果现在感觉被 agent「跟踪」了——它为了调试语音唤醒命令，不停地朝着摄像头喊「HI ESP」。这两件事都生动展示了「让 agent 直接动手」的日常体验。

items.title: Zara Zhang · Builder、Follow Builders 作者
items.summaryEn: Zara Zhang, author of the Follow Builders skill, shared her core belief: agency is the most important human quality. The world will try to box you, label you, and define you—resist that. Notably, this rhymes with the hiring philosophy of Netic founder Melisa Tokmak in this issue's No Priors episode; both treat agency as the single most important signal in a person.
items.insightZh: Follow Builders skill 的作者 Zara Zhang 分享了她的核心信念：能动性（agency）是人最重要的品质。世界会试图把你装进盒子、给你贴标签、替你下定义——要抵抗这一切。有意思的是，这与本期 No Priors 播客里 Netic 创始人 Melisa Tokmak 的招聘哲学高度呼应，两人都把「agency」视为最关键的人才信号。

items.title: How we contain Claude across products
items.summaryEn: Anthropic's engineering team published a full account of how they contain Claude across three agentic products (claude.ai, Claude Code, Claude Cowork). The core principle: design for containment at the environment layer first, then steer behavior at the model layer. They admit that twelve months ago they'd have rejected granting Claude access sufficient to take down an internal service; today that level of access is routine. The piece is full of sobering data and real incidents. Human-in-the-loop approval proved unreliable: telemetry showed users approved roughly 93% of permission prompts, and the more prompts they see the less they scrutinize. An OS-level sandbox (Seatbelt on macOS, bubblewrap on Linux) cut permission prompts by 84%. They walk through three classes of missed risk: vulnerabilities before the trust dialog (an attacker's committed.claude/settings.json hook running before…
items.insightZh: Anthropic 工程团队公开了他们如何在三款 agentic 产品（claude.ai、Claude Code、Claude Cowork）中「围堵」Claude 的完整实践，核心理念是：先在环境层做容器化围堵（containment），再在模型层引导行为。他们坦承十二个月前还会一口回绝「给 Claude 足以搞垮内部服务的权限」，如今这种级别的访问已是常规操作。 文章给出了一组扎心的数据和真实事故。人工审批（human-in-the-loop）并不可靠：遥测显示用户批准了约 93% 的权限提示，审批越多越不上心。为此他们做了 OS 级沙箱（macOS Seatbelt、Linux bubblewrap），把权限提示减少了 84%。他们复盘了三类「踩过的坑」：一是「信任对话框之前」的漏洞——攻击者在仓库里放.claude/settings.json 钩子，在你还没点「信任此文件夹」前就自动执行；二是「用户本身成为注入向量」——一次内部红队钓鱼中，员工被诱导用恶意 prompt 启动 Claude Code，25 次重试里 Claude 成功外泄凭据 24 次；三是「通过被允许的域名外泄」——攻击者在挂载工作区放一个带自己 API key 的文件，Claude 用攻击者的 key 调 Anthropic 的 Files API，数据被上传到攻击者账户，「沙箱完美运行，数据却被外泄了」。 核心教训有三条：优先在环境层做围堵、再在模型层引导；让隔离强度匹配用户的监督能力（会读 bash 的开发者和不会的知识工作者不是同一个威胁模型）；警惕自研组件——身经百战的 hypervisor 和 syscall 过滤器都扛住了，反而是他们自己写的 allowlist 代理出了纰漏。
